title: Sentinel-3C satellite returns first images and measurements
excerpt: The European Space Agency confirmed the satellite is performing well two weeks after its launch.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced on October 8, 2026, that the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite has returned its first images and measurements. The data were collected from two of the satellite's instruments, confirming the spacecraft is functioning as expected following its launch two weeks prior.

The initial imagery includes views of Italy, the Arctic, and the Caribbean captured by the ocean and land colour instrument. Additionally, the synthetic aperture radar altimeter, a tool for measuring surface height, provided data on the Greenland ice sheet and sea surface levels. The altimeter measurements of the Greenland Ice Sheet were acquired between 30 September and 4 October.

The European Space Agency stated that the commissioning phase for the satellite will continue for another five months. Once commissioned, the altimeter will contribute to monitoring changes in sea-surface height around the world, complementing long-term records from missions such as Copernicus Sentinel-6 and Jason.
